passages.paper: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，职业外交官布莱克韦尔勋爵谈到温诺皮亚的政局，又讲了自己怎样走上外交之路，以及外交官需要哪些能力。第二段长对话里，两位同事加班修改一份合同，男士想收工回家，并担心董事会会拖延项目，女士则比较乐观。第一篇短文讲作者处理员工纠纷的经验：真相不明时，不妨往好处想，然后翻篇。第二篇短文讲喜欢做饭的美国人越来越少，在外吃饭花的钱却更多。第一段录音讲托运行李为什么会丢、丢了以后怎么处理。第二段录音介绍一项研究：面对面交谈时只顾看手机，会让对方感到被排斥。第三段录音介绍民宿的兴起，以及开民宿前要考虑的房产、家庭生活方式和收入三个因素。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Today’s special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country’s most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
paras.zh: 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，他是我国经验最丰富、最杰出的职业外交官之一。

paras.en: Welcome.
paras.zh: 欢迎您。

paras.en: It’s my pleasure.
paras.zh: 很荣幸。

paras.en: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
paras.zh: 我们的听众一定特别想了解外交这一行。

paras.en: However, before we talk about that, I’d like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.
paras.zh: 不过，在谈这个之前，我想先问问您今天上了新闻的温诺皮亚共和国的最新动态。

paras.en: What can you tell us?
paras.zh: 您能给我们讲讲吗？

paras.en: I’m afraid I don’t know much beyond what we’ve all seen on the news.
paras.zh: 恐怕我知道的也不比大家在新闻里看到的多。

paras.en: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
paras.zh: 看起来温诺皮亚政府似乎正陷入某种合法性危机，在就国家元首人选达成一致之前，已经成立了一个过渡性的临时政府。

paras.en: But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I’ve never been involved with Winopian relations.
paras.zh: 不过我的工作主要集中在欧洲和美洲这两大洲，所以从来没参与过跟温诺皮亚有关的外交事务。

paras.en: It’s for this reason that I don’t know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，这件事除了报纸上大家都能看到的那些，别的我一概不知。

paras.en: Oh, I see.
paras.zh: 哦，我明白了。

paras.en: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our export envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
paras.zh: 不过请放心，我们驻那里领事馆的专家使节会密切关注局势，我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

w.m: n. 出口；（此处疑为 expert，专家）

paras.en: So, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
paras.zh: 那么，怎样才能从事外交工作呢？

paras.en: There are many different paths one can take.
paras.zh: 可以走的路有很多。

paras.en: All diplomats have their own story, but in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering, followed by six years’ service in the air force.
paras.zh: 每个外交官都有自己的故事，就拿我来说，我先拿了电气工程学位，之后在空军服役了六年。

paras.en: Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps, where I’ve been for 22 years.
paras.zh: 然后我去读了法学院，拿到国际法学位以后，就进了外交使团，到现在已经二十二年了。

paras.en: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
paras.zh: 您认为干这一行最需要哪些关键能力？

paras.en: There are so many.
paras.zh: 太多了。

paras.en: Being a hard worker and good student is important.
paras.zh: 勤奋、好学很重要。

paras.en: You never stop learning.
paras.zh: 学习是永无止境的。

paras.en: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric.
paras.zh: 另外，外交官说话、措辞一定要清楚得体、有说服力。

w.m: adj. 善于表达的；表达清晰的

paras.en: Whether it is diffusing tension or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
paras.zh: 无论是缓和紧张局势，还是推行政策，跟人打交道的能力和沟通能力都至关重要。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第一题：从对话中我们可以了解到这位男士的什么情况？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
paras.zh: 第二题：男士说温诺皮亚政府可能正在经历什么？

paras.en: Question three: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
paras.zh: 第三题：根据男士所说，怎样才能从事外交工作？

paras.en: Question four: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation.
paras.zh: 第四题：对话快结束时，两人主要在讨论什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: It’s getting late, and we’re both displaying signs of weariness, I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
paras.zh: 天不早了，我们俩都累了，我看今天就到这儿吧，明天早上再接着干。

paras.en: Oh, come on, Jeff.
paras.zh: 哎呀，别这样嘛，杰夫。

paras.en: We are so close.
paras.zh: 我们就差一点了。

paras.en: Don’t you think we are almost done?
paras.zh: 你不觉得我们快做完了吗？

paras.en: Let’s do two more hours, please.
paras.zh: 再干两个小时吧，拜托了。

paras.en: One hour, then I’m going home.
paras.zh: 一个小时，干完我就回家。

paras.en: Okay, fine.
paras.zh: 好吧，行。

paras.en: I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们进展很顺利，再改几处，就能全部完成了。

paras.en: I’m sure looking forward to it.
paras.zh: 我真盼着那一刻呢。

paras.en: I’m so tired of this project.
paras.zh: 这个项目我真是受够了。

paras.en: Don’t get me wrong; it’s a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company.
paras.zh: 别误会，这对我来说是个很好的职业机会，对公司来说也是一个里程碑。

paras.en: But it’s just been so long.
paras.zh: 只是拖得实在太久了。

paras.en: Yeah, two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough.
paras.zh: 是啊，两个月来除了这一份合同什么都没干，是有点累人。

paras.en: Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we’ll be done by next week.
paras.zh: 不过，我觉得运气好的话，下周就能完成。

paras.en: You must be delusional.
paras.zh: 你这是在做梦吧。

w.m: adj. 妄想的；不切实际的

paras.en: You don’t think so?
paras.zh: 你不这么觉得吗？

paras.en: No chance.
paras.zh: 不可能。

paras.en: Sections four, five, eight, and nine still have to be aligned to the new framework.
paras.zh: 第四、五、八、九部分还得按新框架调整一致。

paras.en: Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
paras.zh: 然后我们还得把整份校对一遍，确保所有卖点都无懈可击。

w.m: adj. 无懈可击的；严密的

paras.en: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
paras.zh: 不过这些最多也就花几天时间。

paras.en: I wasn’t finished.
paras.zh: 我还没说完呢。

paras.en: When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
paras.zh: 等我们弄完、交到上面以后，你觉得会怎么样？

paras.en: What, they’ll argue about it for like a month?
paras.zh: 他们会为这事争上差不多一个月？

paras.en: There’s always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made.
paras.zh: 总会有那么个把董事插手，要求做些修改。

paras.en: They might think they’re being helpful, but in reality, they’re being obstructive and hampering progress.
paras.zh: 他们可能觉得自己是在帮忙，但实际上是在添乱，拖慢进度。

paras.en: Oh, Jeff, you’re too preoccupied and cynical.
paras.zh: 哎呀，杰夫，你顾虑太多，也太悲观了。

w.m: adj. 心事重重的；想得太多的
adj. 愤世嫉俗的；凡事往坏处想的

paras.en: It won’t be anywhere as bad as that.
paras.zh: 根本不会有那么糟。

w.m: adv. （用于否定）远远（不）；一点也（不）

paras.en: You’ll see.
paras.zh: 等着瞧吧。

paras.en: The entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board too is virtually unanimous in its support.
paras.zh: 整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快落实，董事会也几乎一致支持。

paras.en: Go on, then.
paras.zh: 那好吧。

paras.en: Let’s stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我们就到这儿，明天同一时间再碰头。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士为什么提议今天就到此为止？

paras.en: Question six: What does the woman say is a little tough?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士说什么事有点累人？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they’ll finish by next week?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士认为下周就能完成，男士说她这么想一定是怎么了？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：根据女士的说法，整个管理层希望看到什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: One thing I’ve learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right or wrong solutions to employee disputes.
paras.zh: 我做了二十五年管理工作，学到的一点是：人的行为中存在大量灰色地带，员工之间的纠纷也不一定总有明确的对错之分。

w.m: 二十五年；四分之一世纪

paras.en: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
paras.zh: 两个人对同一件事说法不一的时候，你很难知道该信谁。

paras.en: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
paras.zh: 有一件这样的事，我总会想起来。

paras.en: It happened years ago, and it’s a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
paras.zh: 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突有多容易被忘掉，从这一点就能看出来：我连当时为什么争都不记得了，但怎么解决的，我记得清清楚楚。

paras.en: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we’d never get to the truth.
paras.zh: 两位很有才干的年轻主管，其中一位归我管，他们对同一件事的说法大相径庭，看来我们很可能永远也弄不清真相。

paras.en: We reached a deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, “Here’s something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.”
paras.zh: 我们陷入了僵局，另一位员工的经理说：“我从以前跟过的一位优秀经理那里学到了一句话。”

paras.en: He used to say, “When in doubt, assume positive intent,” and just like that, we had a path forward.
paras.zh: 那位经理常说：“拿不准的时候，就假定对方是出于好意。”就这样，我们一下子找到了出路。

paras.en: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
paras.zh: 我和那位经理都认为，事情的真相我们可能永远也弄不清了。

w.m: n. 职位相当的人；对应的人

paras.en: Quite likely, there were elements of truth in both employees’ stories.
paras.zh: 很可能两位员工的说法都有一部分是真的。

paras.en: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
paras.zh: 我们商定，今后会留意他们的言行和关系，但不再进一步干预。

paras.en: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
paras.zh: 我们把两个人都往好处想，然后就翻篇了。

paras.en: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
paras.zh: 结果，我们把这场冲突抛在了脑后。

paras.en: In fact, their problems didn’t recur.
paras.zh: 事实上，他们的问题再也没有出现过。

paras.en: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
paras.zh: 这些年来，这种通用的做法证明很管用。

paras.en: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
paras.zh: 每当真相不明时，往好处想、商定翻篇，可能是一个有建设性的决定。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?
paras.zh: 第九题：什么时候很难知道该相信谁？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?
paras.zh: 第十题：说话人对作为例子提到的那次纠纷，确切记得的是什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?
paras.zh: 第十一题：两名员工对同一件事说法不一时，说话人和那位经理做了什么？

w.m: n. 职位相当的人；对应的人

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat planned and budgeted for.
paras.zh: 对有些美国人来说，出去吃顿饭是一种早有计划、事先做好预算的享受。

paras.en: For others, it’s just a daily occurrence, and that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
paras.zh: 对另一些人来说，这只是家常便饭，而且随着喜欢做饭的美国人越来越少，后一种人正在成为多数。

paras.en: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans’ attitudes to cooking.
paras.zh: 二十一世纪初，研究人员埃迪·尹做了一项调查，想弄清美国人对做饭的态度。

paras.en: The survey found that 15 percent of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook, and 35% reported mixed feelings.
paras.zh: 调查发现，15%的美国人喜欢做饭，50%说讨厌做饭，35%表示心情复杂。

paras.en: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
paras.zh: 十五年后尹又做了同样的调查，只有10%的受访者说喜欢做饭，45%说讨厌，45%心情复杂。

paras.en: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
paras.zh: 尹认为，做饭和缝纫是一个道理。

paras.en: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
paras.zh: 就在二十世纪初，很多美国人还是自己缝衣服穿。

paras.en: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing.
paras.zh: 如今，绝大多数美国人都买衣服穿。

paras.en: Only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby.
paras.zh: 只有极少数人还自己缝，而且主要是当作一种爱好。

paras.en: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
paras.zh: 尹认为，在家做饭的人也会这样越来越少。

paras.en: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
paras.zh: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上要花三千多美元。

paras.en: However, what people save in convenience they lose in cash.
paras.zh: 然而，人们省了事，却费了钱。

paras.en: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
paras.zh: 就拿上班日买午饭来说吧。

paras.en: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
paras.zh: 买午饭的话，人们平均每顿要花10美元。

paras.en: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
paras.zh: 而自己带午饭，花的钱会少一些。

paras.en: One survey found people only spend, on average, $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
paras.zh: 一项调查发现，从家里带午饭，人们平均只花6.30美元。

paras.en: Americans’ growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
paras.zh: 美国人越来越不愿意花时间待在厨房里，这意味着食品杂货业将面临一系列挑战。

paras.en: It’s likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
paras.zh: 这很可能也会给家庭财务带来不利影响。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do an increasing number of Americans do according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第十二题：根据短文，越来越多的美国人在做什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to?
paras.zh: 第十三题：埃迪·尹认为做饭和什么类似？

paras.en: Question 14: What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch?
paras.zh: 第十四题：美国人自己做午饭，能做到什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America’s grocery industry?
paras.zh: 第十五题：短文说什么意味着美国的食品杂货业将面临一系列挑战？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Every year of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing, and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
paras.zh: 全世界每年托运上飞机的行李有二十五亿多件，其中两千六百万件会丢失，而这两千六百万件里，有一百万件再也回不到原来的主人手里。

paras.en: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
paras.zh: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，还有一些人干脆忘了取走自己的某件行李，都是其中的原因。

paras.en: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don’t know to whom it belongs.
paras.zh: 但行李丢失的头号原因是没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它是谁的。

paras.en: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
paras.zh: 把行李从值机处送到登机口，再到到达口，再到行李提取处，是个很讲究时机的精细活儿。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；需要小心处理的

paras.en: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won’t make connecting flights.
paras.zh: 如果系统运转太慢，行李就赶不上转机航班。

paras.en: If it’s too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
paras.zh: 如果太快，行李可能赶上了转机，乘客却可能误了航班。

paras.en: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
paras.zh: 每个机场都有自己的办法，来分配行李中转需要多长时间。

paras.en: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
paras.zh: 有些机场有先进的自动化系统，包括能读取行李标签的扫描仪、不用停车就能装卸行李的目的地编码运输车，以及能把行李送到相应登机口的分拣机。

paras.en: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
paras.zh: 即便如此，这些技术也未必能保证你的行李标签不会在传送带上被扯掉，那样你就成了一件无名行李的主人。

paras.en: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
paras.zh: 一旦行李丢失、乘客提出索赔，承运人就会宣布这件行李为“处理不当”。

paras.en: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen, or damaged.
paras.zh: “处理不当”指的是延误、丢失、被盗或损坏的行李。

paras.en: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
paras.zh: 大多数延误的行李只比主人晚一个航班，二十四小时内就能送到。

paras.en: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination, if the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
paras.zh: 其他行李由航空公司员工检查，寻找能说明归属和目的地的线索，如果谜团解开了，这些行李会在四五天内还给主人。

paras.en: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
paras.zh: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李会被运到一个中央仓库，在接下来的九十天里经过一整套全面的行李追踪流程。

paras.en: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners’ descriptions.
paras.zh: 航空公司会把这些处理不当的行李登记造册，很多公司还用数据库，把行李里的东西和失主的描述对上号。

paras.en: It takes about three months to go from missing in action to irretrievably lost.
paras.zh: 从“下落不明”到彻底找不回来，大约要三个月。

w.m: （原指士兵）作战中失踪；下落不明

paras.en: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public, so never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage, and make sure your name is on the bag along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
paras.zh: 一旦到了那一步，这些行李就会被捐给慈善机构、拿去拍卖，或者被一家公司买下再卖给公众；所以千万别在托运行李里放真正贵重的东西，还要确保行李上写着你的名字和电话号码，这样工作人员才能联系到你。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is the number one reason a bag ends up lost, according to this talk.
paras.zh: 第十六题：根据这段讲话，行李丢失的头号原因是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems.
paras.zh: 第十七题：即使有先进的自动化系统，你的行李还可能遇到什么情况？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
paras.zh: 第十八题：讲话结束时，说话人建议我们怎么做？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: You’ve probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you’ve probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
paras.zh: 你可能遇到过这样的情况：跟某个人在一起，他却只顾摆弄手机，把你晾在一边；你自己可能也这么干过。

paras.en: In a recent survey, nine out of 10 respondents said they’d used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
paras.zh: 在最近一项调查中，十分之九的受访者说，他们在最近一次社交活动中用过手机。

paras.en: There’s also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
paras.zh: 也有证据表明，这种行为对社交有害。

paras.en: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
paras.zh: 它会让人们对面对面的交流不那么满意，还会引发怨恨和嫉妒。

paras.en: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
paras.zh: 现在，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨产生这些影响的原因。

paras.en: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
paras.zh: 这项研究共有128名参与者，大多是女学生。

paras.en: The participants watched a three-minute animation, in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
paras.zh: 参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画，里面两个卡通人物在互动、交谈。

paras.en: The conversation couldn’t be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
paras.zh: 对话听不到，但可以通过嘴部动作看出来。

paras.en: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
paras.zh: 参与者要把自己想象成视频里离得最近的那个人物，然后对这些对话以及自己对谈话对象的感受作出判断。

paras.en: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant’s conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
paras.zh: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的谈话对象把手机放在桌上，整个谈话过程中一直没用。

paras.en: In another version, their partner’s attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
paras.zh: 在另一个版本中，谈话对象的注意力很快被手机上的什么东西吸引过去，剩下的时间都在摆弄手机。

paras.en: A third version involved the participants’ partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
paras.zh: 第三个版本是，参与者的谈话对象一会儿摆弄手机，一会儿又把手机晾在一边。

paras.en: If you’ve experienced a similar situation, you probably won’t be surprised by the results of the experiments.
paras.zh: 如果你有过类似的经历，大概不会对实验结果感到意外。

paras.en: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
paras.zh: 参与者对社交时使用手机持负面看法。

paras.en: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
paras.zh: 手机出现得越多，他们对互动质量和关系质量的评价就越差。

paras.en: The researchers believed that focusing on one’s phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it’s seen as a form of social exclusion, they assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，之所以会有这种影响，是因为只顾看手机、不理身边的人，会被看作一种社交排斥；他们断言，这种行为就好比一个人不得不在学校食堂独自吃饭。

paras.en: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
paras.zh: 反常之处在于，这种排斥恰恰发生在双方面对面、正在交谈的时候。

w.m: n. 意外转折；反常之处

paras.en: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants’ sense of belonging, need for meaning, and self-esteem.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊心都有不利影响。

paras.en: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
paras.zh: 这些负面影响和传统形式的社交排斥造成的影响类似。

paras.en: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience, this common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment, even as we try to connect with others.
paras.zh: 这些新发现很重要，因为它们让我们更深入地了解了日常生活里一个不起眼却很常见的现象：这种常见的行为会造成恶性循环，让人越来越疏远，即便我们正努力跟别人交流。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；不易察觉的

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about using one’s smartphone during a face-to-face conversation.
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于面对面交谈时用手机，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions.
paras.zh: 第二十题：在这项新研究中，参与者对社交时使用手机有什么反应？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations.
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说，面对面交谈时使用手机这种常见行为会导致什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons, many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
paras.zh: 出于各种原因，越来越多的人外出旅行，很多人是游客，但也有很多人是因私事或公事出门。

paras.en: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
paras.zh: 不管出于什么原因出行，旅行者的一个普遍抱怨是住的地方千篇一律、没有人情味。

w.m: adj. 没有人情味的；冷冰冰的

paras.en: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food, and service are concerned.
paras.zh: 在五家差不多的酒店连住五晚之后，商务旅客可能很难记得每天发生了什么，甚至记不清去过哪些城镇；游客则可能误以为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装修、饮食和服务方面是这样。

paras.en: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed and breakfast arrangements, B and B’s, I mean bed and breakfast arrangements, are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting.
paras.zh: 为了摆脱这种千篇一律、没有人情味的感觉，旅行者开始选择住进当地人家里，也就是住民宿；民宿，我是说提供住宿和早餐的家庭旅馆，就是私人住宅，在非常个性化、温馨友好的环境里为客人提供住宿和早餐。

w.m: adj. 没有人情味的；冷冰冰的
住宿加早餐（的旅馆）；民宿

paras.en: For decades, B and B’s have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles, and in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
paras.zh: 几十年来，民宿一直是游览欧洲、尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式；其实在美国，这也不算什么新鲜主意。

paras.en: The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
paras.zh: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，那时客栈很少，疲惫的旅人只能指望陌生人好心给一顿饭、一张床。

paras.en: But the revival of B and B’s as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
paras.zh: 但民宿作为一种受欢迎的住处重新兴起，是近些年才有的现象。

w.m: adj. 令人向往的；理想的

paras.en: If the idea of operating a B and B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
paras.zh: 如果你对经营民宿感兴趣，那么在投身这一行之前，有几个因素需要考虑。

paras.en: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself but the location.
paras.zh: 首先要考虑的是你的房产，不只是房子本身，还有地段。

paras.en: If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination such as New York City or Washington D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B and B.
paras.zh: 如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或者住在纽约市、华盛顿特区这样的热门目的地，那么你的房子就算相当简单，开民宿照样能经营得不错。

paras.en: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath, or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
paras.zh: 另一方面，如果你的房子建筑风格独特，或者有方便旅客的设施，比如独立入口、独立浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意跑上一段路来找你。

paras.en: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
paras.zh: 另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。

paras.en: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry, and bookkeeping involved.
paras.zh: 你必须考虑：家里所有人是不是真的喜欢有客人来，愿不愿意一遍遍地介绍当地景点和活动，有没有时间和精力应付随之而来的额外做饭、打扫、洗衣和记账。

paras.en: The final consideration is a financial one.
paras.zh: 最后要考虑的是钱的问题。

paras.en: Potential B and B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
paras.zh: 想开民宿的人必须对能赚多少钱有现实的预期。

paras.en: While B and B’s usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B and B.
paras.zh: 虽然民宿的初期成本通常很低，但专家估计，房东至少要有五间房经常租出去，才能靠民宿维持生计。

paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人说旅行者通常抱怨什么？

paras.zh: 如果你想做民宿生意，首先要考虑的是什么？

paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人说想开民宿的人必须对什么有现实的预期？
